rows.49:08a8:
Wait a moment.
If I'm telling the fourth story, there's no need to go all the way back to the newspaper club.
The story I meant to tell is about this cherry tree, too.
...My name is Akemi Iwashita.
I'm a third-year.
I must say, my heart skipped a beat when Fukuzawa chose the cherry tree for the third story.
I couldn't believe that a first-year like you would know a story about this cherry tree.
After all, this story was a legend known only to a very select few.
...But I'm glad.
Glad that Fukuzawa's story was a lie.
Wherever did you hear that story about this cherry tree?
Some of it may well be accurate, but what on earth did you hear that let you make up a story like that?
Perhaps you have a gift for writing fiction, Fukuzawa.
Or are you simply a swindler?
...Please don't be angry with me.
I'm only telling the truth.
This place was a dumping ground for corpses during the war, you say?
This cherry tree was forced to watch horrifying sights, over and over, you say?
During the war, they threw living people away along with the dead?
That is ridiculous beyond words.
Besides, even if it were true, there are countless sights far more horrifying than that.{p}
rows.49:0fd8:
It's true that this cherry tree is steeped in a grudge.
Many grudges, in fact.
But they don't belong to the soldiers who died in the war, nor to the warlords who died in the Warring States period.
It's something else...
They're grudges born of the fierce, wicked attachment that people living perfectly ordinary lives felt for this world.
{a}{f:|}?
What you saw a little while ago was that grudge.
Not the soldiers who died in the war.
Now I'll tell you the truth.
The story of the real grudge that has taken hold of this cherry tree.
In return, will you make me a promise?
No matter what happens, you won't move from this spot until my story is over.
And you will never, ever scream.
Understood?{p}Can you promise me that?
rows.49:2490:
At ten o'clock on the night of the full moon, the two met at the school's back gate.
It was a quiet night, without a soul around.
Of course, both of them had sneaked out of their homes.
If they'd told their families the truth, they would never have been allowed to go.
"Have you been waiting long?"
"No, I just got here."
Though each was sure the other would come, they had both been uneasy until they reached the back gate.
When they spotted each other, they ran to each other at the same moment and took each other's hands.
And they nodded together.
It was a signal to confirm their resolve.{p}
rows.49:2cdc:
"I couldn't see their faces. Could you, Orihara?"
Hirooka asked anxiously.
She only shook her head quietly.
At that, he made his decision.
He would keep quiet.
"Let's keep this a secret between just the two of us. That way, they're sure to convince themselves they only imagined seeing us.
And then they won't have to suffer any misfortune, will they?"
By saying so, Hirooka convinced himself as well.
In fact, perhaps that really was the best thing.
Orihara, too, decided to go along with Hirooka.
And so the two of them came to share a secret.
Having a secret of your own, just between two people, is important, you know.
When a man and a woman share a secret, their relationship moves forward quickly.
Perhaps the legend of the cherry tree was born from that very idea in the first place.
And then they parted, promising that tomorrow night, without fail, they would confirm their love once more.{p}
rows.49:33ec:
Even so, they found it hard to go to the cherry tree.
As for carrying out that legend, they were in no mood for anything of the kind.
Still, when they thought of the two who had died believing they'd been seen, they couldn't bear to be alone.
"...It's my fault. Because I ran away that time, they died. ...If I'd explained what happened then, those two might not have had to die."
Head bowed, Hirooka spoke weakly.
Orihara just cried in silence.
To be honest, the two of them had no idea what they should do from then on.
And that was when it happened.{p}
rows.49:395c:
I see.
You're surprisingly innocent, aren't you?
The two of them gave that answer, too.
Their consciences must have been tormenting them terribly.
"...It's true, I'm the one to blame. If I can, I want to take responsibility. ...What should I do?"
That was the answer Hirooka gave, I'm afraid.
The voice that replied sounded pleased.{p}
rows.49:4a30:
I'm sorry, but this is a story I can only tell to people who've made me that promise.
As for why, you'd only understand that by hearing the story itself, so I can't explain it to you.
That's how frightening a story it is.
So, I'm afraid I can't tell it to you.
But if you ever want to hear it, let me know.
When you do, don't be shy. Just say, "I promise, so please tell me."
I'll tell it to you anytime.
So that's as far as my story goes...
Now, shall we go back to the club room?{p}
rows.49:73c0:
Then, after school exactly one week after that night, he worked up the nerve to talk to her.
"I'm sorry to bring this up again myself after what I said, but..."
"It's all right. It's been bothering me too, so much that I can't sleep at night. I was just about to bring it up myself."
It seems both of them had been dying to talk about that night.
"I'm thinking of going back to that cherry tree once more. I have something in mind, too...
And the cherry tree did say we must come... What will you do, Orihara?"
"...I'll go too. I don't think there's anything to worry about as long as you're with me, Hirooka... I really don't think that voice was a dream. I wonder if maybe it was the voice of that cherry tree..."
And so they decided to meet at the back gate at ten o'clock that night.{p}
rows.49:7f1c:
The flames burned more fiercely than they had expected, and the two of them couldn't move...
Beyond the shimmering heat haze, she felt as if those two from before smiled for an instant.
The fire caught their clothes and charred their skin with a sizzle, giving off a foul smell...
The two of them writhed in agony until they breathed their last.
And then, from somewhere, came that voice.
"You have taken responsibility properly, haven't you? That is what taking responsibility must mean..."{p}
rows.49:8a00:
Hirooka, on the other hand, was listening to what the cherry tree was saying as if he were hypnotized.
Orihara was able to watch the scene calmly.
When she looked into his eyes, he seemed to be pretty far gone.
Uneasy at a scene that, however you looked at it, boded nothing good, Orihara grabbed his shoulder.
"Hirooka, please come to your senses!
There's no telling what will happen if you do what the cherry tree says, here and now!
Please! Come back, come back to yourself!"
His eyes, which seemed to be staring into the distance, showed no sign of coming back.
Even so, she kept shaking his shoulders and hitting him.
All she could think about was getting out of there with him, even one second sooner.
Just then, he turned toward her, as if something had suddenly occurred to him.
"Let's get away from here, quick!"
She took his hand and started to run.
At that moment, he squeezed her hand as hard as he could.
And he didn't run at all; he just stayed right where he was.{p}
rows.49:987c:
It's simple.
Because I am the servant of this cherry tree... no, of those two...
Those two appear in my dreams almost every night.
I started having those dreams when I was a first-year.
And those two tell me stories.
I've sat on a branch of the cherry tree and listened to all kinds of stories.
Almost every single night, the stories those two tell unfold in my dreams in vivid images.
Every night, their agony-filled faces appear right before my eyes, filling my sight...
No matter how tightly I shut my eyes, those faces of terror float up through my eyelids, always staring at me.{p}
rows.49:9de0:
Ah, I can feel something!
The cherry tree... those two are speaking to me!
What is it you want to say?
What are you trying to tell me?
...Oh, is that so? Really?
I understand...
It seems those two have chosen you to take over after me.
I can tell...
Those two seem pleased about it, too.
About the birth of a new servant...
If you don't believe it, that's fine. You'll just end up the sacrifice yourself, that's all.
And you'll see that dream every night, too.
And their faces of terror, as well.
Don't worry, you'll get used to it soon.
Oh, and there was a promise you made me earlier, remember?
Thank you for keeping it.
Keeping that promise was one of the conditions for being chosen, you see.{p}
